newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Elitbank to raise capital to 4.0 bln levs.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Elitbank to raise capital to 4.0 bln levs.

text.p: Bulgaria's private Elitbank, in receivership since September, on Monday decided to raise capital to 4.0 billion levs from 1.0 billion levs, a bank official said.

"The shareholders' meeting today voted for a capital rise to four billion levs through a new share issue to meet central bank minimum capital requirements," the official who declined to be named, told Reuters.
Austria's CHL investment company had bought a five percent stake in the current bank's capital and had applied to acquire 50.50 percent after the rise, the official said.
CHL submitted the application at the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) on December 6 and a decision could be expected by June 6 at the latest, said the official.
Elitbank planned to change strategy and develop as a corporate bank after completing its stabilisation programme, the official said.

The BNB placed Elitbank in receivership on September 23, saying it was in danger of insolvency due to a capital-to-risk assets ratio of minus 2.42 percent on August 31 and outstanding payments of 261 million levs as of September 20.
The BNB also dismissed its management and appointed sequestrators to establish the bank's financial state.

Eight other local state and private banks were also put in receivership on September 23 due to negative capital-to-risk assets ratios ranging between 9.95 percent and 56.6 percent and outstanding payments totalling 11.10 billion levs, BNB figures showed.
The BNB has sought insolvency for those eight banks through the courts but has not opened a bankruptcy procedure for Elitbank so far.
Under the latest BNB requirements Bulgaria's commercial banks should have a minimum capital of 1.4 billion levs for a domestic licence and 2.2 billion levs for a full one by March 31, 1997.
